dim_resolution.structure: flat_array<int32> (expected ~4 ids); use linear scan or unordered_set

join_order.filter: kind_id == kt_id AND production_year != INT32_MIN AND production_year > 2010
join_order.notes: kind_id selectivity ~7% (movies); production_year>2010 ~12%; combined ~1-3% of 2.5M titles -> ~50-100K. Cardinality estimate is conservative.
For each surviving title mv, scan mk[mkmid[mv]..mkmid[mv+1]); check keyword_id in k_ids (linear scan over ~4 ids is cache-friendly). Break on first match.
For each surviving title mv, scan mi[mimid[mv]..mimid[mv+1]); require info_type_id==it1_id AND info in country set. Use length-prefix dispatch then memcmp. Break on first match.

For each surviving title mv, scan mi_idx[mixmid[mv]..mixmid[mv+1]); require info_type_id==it2_id AND lex_lt(info, '8.5'). For each surviving row update MIN(mi_idx.info) and MIN(t.title). Note: a single title may match multiple mi_idx rows; aggregate MIN over all surviving (t,mi_idx) pairs.

filters.predicate: info_type_id==it1_id AND info IN (10 country strings)

data_structures.min_rating: std::string (or string_view tracking best mi_idx row)
data_structures.min_title: std::string (or string_view tracking best title row)

parallelism.reduction: per-thread (min_rating_local, min_title_local); final reduction takes lex-min across threads
parallelism.notes: Title scan drives ~2.5M rows; each title independently probes mk/mi/mi_idx via offsets. Embarrassingly parallel. 12 cores available.

output.notes: Scalar aggregate; emits a single row. Note MIN(t.title) is over the same multiset of (t,mi_idx) pairs as MIN(mi_idx.info), but since they aggregate independently over the join output, equivalent to MIN(t.title) over titles that pass all four semi/inner conditions.

ordering_rationale: Title is the natural driver: it is the central node of the star join, has filterable predicates (kind, year), and all three fact tables have offsets_only indexes keyed by movie_id. Ordering the existence semi-joins as mk(small fan-out, ~2) -> mi(fan-out ~6) -> mi_idx(fan-out ~0.5) puts the most selective and cheapest existence check first. mi_idx is last because it actually produces aggregation tuples rather than acting as a filter.
